title: Modules Strings Shade

# PV102 Day 4: Module Behavior String Design and Shade

Students connect PV101 series/parallel measurement habits to PV102 design judgment: string voltage, current, controller limits, temperature, and shade-sensitive layout decisions.

PV102 | CTS Day 20 | Instructor Run Sheet

String design follows limits, temperature, and shade reality. | Thursday, August 6, 2026

# Core rule

String design follows limits, temperature, and shade reality.

# Learning targets

Predict how series and parallel wiring affect PV string voltage and current.

Explain why controller input limits control string design.

Recognize shade as both a production and mismatch problem.

Use a safe paper/string model to compare design options before hardware work.

# Readiness and materials

| Before students arrive | Materials |
| --- | --- |
| Open slide deck and test display. Print student packets and one instructor key. Prepare three team stations. Review safety boundary before any equipment is handled. | PV module spec sheet samples ; String cards ; Calculator ; Shade cards ; Controller limit cards ; Whiteboard ; Projector and slide deck |

# Five-hour run of show

| Time | Block | Instructor move |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 10:00-10:15 | Opening and continuity | Connect Day 3 to today's rule. Name what students already know and what new judgment is being added. |
| 10:15-10:40 | Morning quiz and review | Students work independently for 12-15 minutes. Review by asking for evidence, not just letters. |
| 10:40-11:25 | Concept lesson | Use slides 1-14. Pause after each technical rule and ask what decision it changes. |
| 11:25-12:15 | Guided practice | Model one example on the board. Students complete a quick pair-check before lunch. |
| 12:15-12:45 | Lunch/reset | Reset lab stations. Keep energized work out of scope unless explicitly authorized by instructor and equipment procedure. |
| 12:45-1:00 | Lab brief | Assign teams and roles. Review acceptance criteria and stop-work triggers. |
| 1:00-2:15 | String Design Paper Lab | Teams compare three paper string options against controller limits and shade constraints. |
| 2:15-2:40 | Handoffs and peer verification | Each team gives a concise technical handoff. Peers check evidence, boundary, and unknowns. |
| 2:40-3:00 | Exit ticket and reset | Collect packets. Preview next step: PV102 Day 5 turns daily energy need into storage, autonomy, and battery-protection decisions. |

# Instructor talk track

Opening script: "PV102 is not about throwing parts at a problem until reality files a complaint. Today we use module behavior string design and shade to make the next design decision safer and more defensible. The rule is simple: String design follows limits, temperature, and shade reality."

# Teaching notes

| Move | Look-for |
| --- | --- |
| Ask | What decision does this evidence change? |
| Listen for | Students separating facts, assumptions, and unknowns. |
| Correct gently | Component-first answers. Redirect to job, evidence, boundary, then component. |
| Require | A handoff that another person could act on without reading minds. Humanity keeps trying telepathy. It remains a poor project-management system. |

# Lab instructor procedure

Read the module and controller cards.

Build three possible string layouts using cards.

Calculate approximate operating voltage/current and open-circuit voltage.

Mark shade exposure from Day 2 scenario notes.

Reject any option that violates a limit or ignores shade evidence.

Handoff the safest first-pass string layout and its required verification checks.

# Answer snapshot and contingency plan

If equipment or printing is unavailable, run the lab with paper cards, chart paper, and oral handoffs. The learning target is decision quality, not hardware theater.

# Safety and scope boundaries

No live electrical work is authorized by this lesson unless the instructor independently sets up a verified training system, follows manufacturer instructions, and establishes the required isolation, PPE, and supervision. Treat PV source circuits and batteries as energy sources, not props.

# Day handoff

PV102 Day 5 turns daily energy need into storage, autonomy, and battery-protection decisions.
